synthesis: At deterministic depth n, derive independence of generated history from unused iid input clocks via finite-prefix measurability. The source does not assume arbitrary random histories are independent, does not state a random-stopping-tail theorem, and does not obtain the full A.7 expansion from independence alone.

source_printed.restatement: Fix y, reference point and initial phase-space point. Draw independent unit exponential clocks. The next wait is the first nonnegative time when integrated flow intensity reaches the next clock. For a finite wait, add its duration and bounce the flowed state. An empty crossing set gives infinite next wait/time and stops recursion; between events follow the flow.

Energy preservation gives a finite rate cap depending on fixed parameters and initial energy. A zero cap gives no jumps. For a positive cap, each finite wait is bounded below by its clock divided by the cap; on the nonterminating branch the strong law makes event times diverge almost surely. Memorylessness is invoked for the homogeneous Markov property.

For fixed horizon t and n prescribed strictly ordered event times, form the flow/bounce path. The author attributes its event-time density to iteration of the clocks: a full-path survival exponential times all pre-bounce intensities. Sum these n-event integrals to obtain bounded measurable path-functional expectations. The rate cap and simplex volume give absolute convergence.

objects_domains_quantifiers.fixed_source_inputs: Euclidean position/momentum; fixed y, reference point and deterministic initial state; positive eta. The paper assumes a C2 potential with positive lower and finite upper Hessian bounds, and eta in (0,1/beta]. The local independence lemma does not need convexity or a specific rate.
objects_domains_quantifiers.probability_inputs: One probability law and a mutually independent family E_j, j>=1, each Exp(1). Pairwise independence alone is insufficient for block/tail independence.
objects_domains_quantifiers.deterministic_depth: For every fixed n>=0, F_n=sigma(E_1,...,E_n). Generated history H_n must be F_n-measurable, derived from the recursion as an internal dependency rather than added as a public PBPS source premise.
objects_domains_quantifiers.history_carrier: On the live nth-event branch, history can contain past waits, event times and post-bounce states. For a global random variable use a tagged stopped/infinite branch rather than invent a phase-space state at infinity. Stopped flags through stage n use only the first n clocks.
objects_domains_quantifiers.unused_tail: Tail_n=(E_(n+1+k))_(k>=0) with its countable product Borel sigma algebra. Next-clock-only independence suffices for one-step factorization; whole-tail independence is a reusable strengthening.
objects_domains_quantifiers.random_initialization: The printed expectation fixes the initial state. A random initial-state extension requires joint independence of that state from the clock family, with the initial state included in the past sigma algebra. Clock iid alone does not establish this.

implicit_required_derivation.claim: Finite generated recursion is measurable in its consumed clock prefix, including alive/stopped alternatives.
implicit_required_derivation.justification: Integrated hazard is continuous and nondecreasing in time and Borel in parameters. Threshold crossing is extended-time Borel; Borel flow and bounce then give finite measurable composition. The later A.2 paragraph gives a joint-Borel recursion argument; the prefix restriction follows from A.1/A.2 indices.

implicit_required_derivation.claim: For each deterministic n, sigma(E_1,...,E_n) is independent of sigma(E_(n+1),E_(n+2),...).
implicit_required_derivation.justification: Mutual family independence factors disjoint finite-coordinate cylinders; a pi-lambda or monotone-class argument extends independence to the generated sigma algebras.
implicit_required_derivation.consumer: Independence descends to a measurable function of the prefix and any measurable tail function.

implicit_required_derivation.claim: H_n and Tail_n are independent. In particular E_(n+1) retains its unit exponential conditional law given H_n or F_n.
implicit_required_derivation.justification: Apply the two independent sigma algebras to the finite-prefix measurable history. Do not assume independence for a history that inspects unused clocks.
implicit_required_derivation.consumer: Conditional next-wait factors in the finite-event iteration.

implicit_required_derivation.classification: additional source-implicit distributional edge, beyond independence alone
implicit_required_derivation.claim: On a live finite nth event, conditional next-wait survival through u is exp(-A_(Z_n)(u)), where A_z is integrated flow intensity.
implicit_required_derivation.justification: S_(n+1)>u iff E_(n+1)>A_(Z_n)(u) almost surely, and use the independent exponential law. Flat hazard intervals are permitted. The random hazard threshold is past-measurable and requires measurable-parameter product integration.
implicit_required_derivation.consumer: Each next-event law and the final no-event survival factor.

implicit_required_derivation.classification: future consumer not discharged by the independence edge
implicit_required_derivation.claim: Derive finite-wait density lambda(Phi_u Z_n) exp(-A_(Z_n)(u)), retain infinite-wait mass exp(-A_(Z_n)(infinity)), iterate at deterministic event depth and sum using non-explosion.
implicit_required_derivation.justification: These are further distributional, integration and countable decomposition steps behind the printed A.7 iteration.
implicit_required_derivation.consumer: Complete A.7, followed by A.8 trajectory reversal and subsequent invariance/semigroup conclusions.

conditioning_sense.minimal: For measurable B,C, P(H_n in B and E_(n+1) in C)=P(H_n in B)P(E_(n+1) in C). Equivalently for bounded measurable f, conditional expectation of f(E_(n+1)) given F_n is its constant expectation almost surely.
conditioning_sense.tail: For full-tail claims extend from cylinder events to every event of the countable product sigma algebra; a finite-tail claim alone does not state this extension.
conditioning_sense.exact_histories: A particular continuous-valued history can have probability zero. Conditioning is an almost-everywhere conditional expectation/regular conditional law or kernel identity, never division by that point-event probability.
conditioning_sense.random_thresholds: A_(Z_n)(u) is random and F_n-measurable. Its conditional survival evaluation needs the joint product law or a measurable-parameter integration result, not only a fixed-threshold identity.

deterministic_depth_vs_stopping.required: A.7 uses fixed n and deterministic ordered event times. Its local probability bridge needs deterministic-depth past versus unused inputs.
deterministic_depth_vs_stopping.optional_valid_extension: If K is an almost surely finite stopping index for F_n, shifted clocks after K are independent of the stopped sigma algebra; prove by partitioning on K=n. This is separate and unnecessary for fixed-n A.7 iteration.
deterministic_depth_vs_stopping.invalid_default: An arbitrary random history/index may reveal a future clock. The event count N_t before physical time t uses whether E_(N_t+1) exceeds the accumulated hazard. Given that survival information, the original next clock is truncated, not an unchanged independent exponential.
deterministic_depth_vs_stopping.physical_time_residual: Memorylessness applies to E_(n+1)-A_(Z_n)(t-T_n), conditional on survival and past, through a separate conditional argument. It does not make the original clock independent of the observed survival history.
deterministic_depth_vs_stopping.nontermination: Conditioning on never terminating can inspect infinitely many clocks. The non-explosion proof intersects a probability-one SLLN event with this branch and needs no unused-tail independence conditional on that branch.

stopping_endpoint_conventions: An empty crossing set gives infinite wait/time and no defined later bounced phase state. This is stopping rather than explosion.
A finite total integrated hazard allows an atom at infinite wait. The finite-event density need not have mass one; final survival accounts for no further event before a finite horizon.

Crossing uses >= at nonnegative times. Exponential clocks are positive almost surely and locally bounded intensities imply positive finite waits; threshold equalities are conditionally null once independence is established.
The simplex uses 0<t_1<...<t_n<t. Events exactly at deterministic endpoints are null under the finite-wait laws. The n=0 case uses empty product one and zero-dimensional integration.
A zero rate cap gives no events. Non-explosion excludes infinite events in finite physical time almost surely, while infinite sequences over infinite time remain possible.
failure_boundary: H=E_(n+1) is a direct counterexample to independence for arbitrary history.
Mutual independence cannot silently be weakened to pairwise independence.
A private default state after stopping is not source semantics; use tagged or branch-restricted interfaces.
This local probability bridge alone proves neither non-explosion nor Markovness, A.7, invariance or a complete paper theorem.
candidate_acceptance: Derive independence from independent clocks plus consumed-prefix measurability; do not accept unexplained history/next-clock independence as a new source-facing hypothesis.
Use deterministic n or separately establish a valid stopping-index condition; the history must not inspect clocks beyond n.
Keep the probability measure, sigma algebra, measurable carriers and index offset explicit.
Represent stopped/infinite branches without asserting a finite next jump.
Claim only a source-implicit probability dependency unless actual PBPS history composition and later event-law integration are compiled and reviewed.
scope_exclusions: A.4-A.6 analytic/change-of-variables mechanisms are not new probability dependencies in this bounded slice.
